title: The Collected Works of Edgar Allan Poe, Volume I: Poems
publisher: Belknap Press of Harvard University Press
reliability_notes: The standard scholarly text of Poe's poems, reconstructing each poem from the manuscripts, the early printings and Poe's own revisions, with exhaustive textual and source notes. Volumes II and III (Tales and Sketches) appeared later, in 1978, so this volume should be cited on its own date.

title: The Letters of Edgar Allan Poe (2 volumes)
reliability_notes: The first collected edition of Poe's correspondence, with editorial notes and identification of recipients and sources; long the basis for documentary work on Poe's career and finances. Later censuses and editions add letters and correct readings, so individual items should be checked against them.

title: David Walker's Appeal to the Coloured Citizens of the World
reliability_notes: The standard scholarly edition of Walker's 1829-1830 Appeal, with a substantial introduction, annotation and documentary appendices on the editions and the reaction to the pamphlet. The text follows Walker's own third edition rather than the modernised reprints.

title: The History of Mary Prince, a West Indian Slave, Related by Herself
reliability_notes: The revised and expanded edition of Prince's narrative with Ferguson's introduction and notes drawn from Bermuda and London archives; the usual scholarly text for the narrative and its editorial framing by Thomas Pringle. Its account of the composition has been qualified by later work on the transcript by Susanna Strickland.

title: Stedman's Surinam: Life in an Eighteenth-Century Slave Society. An Abridged, Modernized Edition of Narrative of a Five Years Expedition against the Revolted Negroes of Surinam
reliability_notes: The Prices' abridged and modernised rendering of Stedman's 1796 narrative, with introduction and notes, and the practical scholarly route into a difficult and much-altered text. Because it abridges and modernises, quotations should be checked against the unabridged 1796 edition or the Prices' later full translation.

title: The Letters of William Lloyd Garrison, Volume I: I Will Be Heard!, 1822-1835
publisher: Belknap Press of Harvard University Press
reliability_notes: The opening volume of the definitive Garrison correspondence, covering the founding of The Liberator and the formation of the American Anti-Slavery Society, with full annotation. Later volumes continue the series, so citations should give the volume and years rather than the series alone.

title: Travels in New England and New York (4 volumes)
author_or_editor: Barbara Miller Solomon (editor, with the assistance of Patricia M. King)
reliability_notes: The annotated modern edition of Dwight's topographical and statistical survey, the standard scholarly text for citations of the Travels and its later issues. It follows the New Haven printing of 1821-1823 rather than the earlier first volumes, so page numbers differ from the 1790s editions.

title: Lydia Sigourney: Selected Poetry and Prose (Broadview Editions)
reliability_notes: A critical selection spanning Sigourney's career, with introduction, textual notes and explanatory annotation, useful for teaching and for her occasional and reform prose as well as the lyric poems. It is a selection, not a complete edition, so individual poems must be checked against the collected Poems of 1834 and later editions.

title: Observations on American Art: Selections from the Writings of John Neal (1793-1876)
reliability_notes: Number 12 of the Pennsylvania State College Studies series; collects Neal's scattered criticism of American painting and art institutions, including the artist reviews first printed in Blackwood's and in American periodicals. It is selective and lightly annotated, so its text should be verified against the original periodical printings.

title: The Life of Washington (The John Harvard Library)
publisher: Belknap Press of Harvard University Press
reliability_notes: The first scholarly edition of Weems's best-selling Life of Washington, with Cunliffe's introduction and notes tracing the successive editions and the invention of the cherry-tree story. It edits one stage of a text that Weems repeatedly rewrote, so quotations need checking against the specific early edition.

title: The Letters and Journals of James Fenimore Cooper (6 volumes)
publisher: Belknap Press of Harvard University Press
reliability_notes: The collected Cooper correspondence and journals, issued between 1960 and 1968, with detailed editorial notes on persons, places and publications; the standard documentary source for Cooper's career, his European years and his publishing dealings. Volume dates differ across the set, so a citation should name the volume.

title: A Common Heritage: Noah Webster's Blue-Back Speller
reliability_notes: A book-length study of Webster's spelling book and its readers, with a careful bibliography of editions and printing history; the standard starting point for the American Spelling Book and for Webster's educational writings. Its attention is on the speller rather than on the dictionary or the grammars.

title: A New-England Tale (Penguin Classics)
author_or_editor: Susan K. Harris (introduction) and Emily Van Dette (notes)
reliability_notes: The annotated modern text of Sedgwick's first novel of 1822, with Harris's introduction on its Unitarian and political contexts and Van Dette's explanatory notes. It prints the first-edition text and is a single-volume edition rather than part of a complete Sedgwick.

title: The Complete Works of Washington Irving (30 volumes)
author_or_editor: Henry A. Pochmann, Herbert L. Kleinfield and Richard D. Rust (general editors)
reliability_notes: The centenary collected edition of Irving, issued from 1969 through the mid-1980s with textual and bibliographical apparatus and separate volumes of letters and journals; the basis for scholarly reference to individual titles and their variant printings. Volumes appeared over many years and were variously issued with Twayne, so each title needs its own citation.

title: The Poetical Works of Fitz-Greene Halleck: Now First Collected
reliability_notes: The first collected edition of Halleck's verse, assembling the narrative poems such as Crooked Creek and Alrazzi with the shorter pieces, and the fullest collection issued in his lifetime. Later nineteenth-century printings added and reordered material, so its contents are not identical to the posthumous editions.

title: The Prose Writings of William Cullen Bryant (2 volumes)
reliability_notes: Bryant's critical, editorial and travel prose collected by his son-in-law shortly after his death, with Godwin's biographical sketch of his life and opinions; the standard source for his reviews and editorials before the later scholarly editions. Godwin selects and silently reprints, so periodical first printings should be checked for wording and dates.

title: Joel Barlow's Columbiad: A Bicentennial Reading
reliability_notes: A book-length critical study of Barlow's 1807 revision of The Vision of Happiness into The Columbiad, with a reprint discussion of the poem's politics, its front matter and its plate illustrations. It treats the 1807 poem rather than the earlier Vision of 1787, so citations of Barlow's own text should give the edition used.

title: William Ellery Channing: An Essay on the Liberal Spirit in America
reliability_notes: An intellectual biography of Channing that situates the Unitarian writings, the sermons and the Reviews-and-Almanack circle within early nineteenth-century American letters; the standard scholarly study for citations about Channing's prose and reputation. It is a study, not an edition, so Channing's texts themselves must be cited from the sermons and the collected works.

title: Selections from the Writings and Speeches of William Lloyd Garrison. With an Appendix
reliability_notes: Garrison's own anthology of his speeches, letters and Liberator editorials through the early 1850s, issued in Boston by his agent R. F. Wallcut with an appendix on the split in the abolitionist movement. The selections are abridged and re-set by Garrison himself, so wording and dates must be checked against the original Liberator printings.

title: An Essay on the Slavery and Commerce of the Human Species, Particularly the African, Translated from a Latin Dissertation, Which Was Honoured with the First Prize in the University of Cambridge, for the Year 1785
reliability_notes: A Cambridge Library Collection - Slavery and Abolition facsimile of Clarkson's prizewinning Latin essay as translated and published in 1786, issued with the appended Thoughts upon the African Slave Trade and John Newton's letter as in the early editions. Being a facsimile it retains the original pagination and spelling, so it can stand in for the 1786 printing in quotations.

title: Pamphlets on West Indian Slavery
reliability_notes: A Cambridge Library Collection - Slavery and Abolition facsimile volume (published September 2010) that reprints Heyrick's Immediate not Gradual Abolition of 1824 together with a contemporary pamphlet arguing the opposing gradual-abolition case. It reproduces the pamphlets as printed, so pagination and spelling differ from the separate early editions.

title: A Narrative of the Life and Adventures of Venture, a Native of Africa: But Resident above Sixty Years in the United States of America. Related by Himself
publisher: Printed by C. Holt, at the Bee-Office, New-London, Connecticut
reliability_notes: The original printing of Smith's narrative, the earliest New England slave narrative and a foundational text of the abolition strand, issued in New London in 1798 and reprinted in facsimile in modern collections. The preface and much of the wording were shaped by the white compiler Elisha N. Dimond, so the narrative should be read as an edited relation of Smith's own testimony.

title: James Kirke Paulding: The Last Republican
reliability_notes: A volume in the Contributions in American History series and the only book-length study of Paulding, tracing his Dutch-themed fiction, his political prose and his long public career from the Knickerbicker period to the Pierce presidency. It relies on Paulding's published works and on manuscript collections, so its dating of individual items still needs checking against the editions themselves.

title: The Life, Travels, and Opinions of Benjamin Lundy: Including His Journeys to Texas and Mexico; with a Sketch of Contemporary Events, and a Notice of the Revolution in Hayti
reliability_notes: Lundy's own anthology of his writing published in Philadelphia a year before his death, gathering the early abolitionist essays, the Texas and Mexico journey narrative and the material on Haiti from the Genius of Universal Emancipation. It is a selection arranged by Lundy himself, so the items reappear in their original periodical form with different pagination.

title: Early American Drama
reliability_notes: An anthology of eight early United States plays, including Barker's The Indian Princess: A Melodrama of 1808, edited with an introduction and explanatory notes that situate the dramas in theatrical and political context. The texts are modernised and lightly edited selections rather than complete scholarly editions, so first-printing variants must be consulted separately.

title: An Appeal in Favor of That Class of Americans Called Africans
reliability_notes: Karcher's critical edition of Child's 1833 Appeal, the founding argument for immediate emancipation in American print, reprinted with her introduction and notes tracing the book's reception and the censure it brought its author. It reprints the first edition, so the enlarged later editions of the 1830s differ in wording and arrangement.

title: Maria W. Stewart, America's First Black Woman Political Writer: Essays and Speeches
reliability_notes: Richardson's scholarly collection of Stewart's 1830s meditations, addresses and letters, first gathered from the Liberator and other abolitionist prints, with an introduction establishing her place in early Black political oratory. It is a selection of the speeches and essays rather than her complete writings, so individual texts should be checked against their periodical first printings.

title: The Diplomatic Correspondence of the American Revolution (12 volumes)
reliability_notes: Sparks' documentary edition of the letters of Franklin, Deane, John Adams and other American diplomats abroad, prepared from official papers and the first major edited correspondence of the Revolution. The volumes were issued between 1829 and 1830, and later archival editions of these diplomats' papers supersede parts of the text and annotation.

title: The Geography Made Easy: Being a New Abridgement of the American Universal Geography
reliability_notes: The school abridgement of Morse's American Universal Geography, the geography textbook that standardised physical and political geography in early American classrooms and ran through many revised issues. The editions differ substantially from printing to printing as Morse added new material, so a citation should give the specific imprint used.

title: Sketches of American Character
reliability_notes: Hale's first book, tales and character sketches first issued in parts in the mid-1820s and gathered here into a single Boston volume, the usual text for her early fiction and its portraits of sectional character. The parts and the early editions were revised and reissued by other publishers, so quotations should be checked against the specific printing.

title: Modern Chivalry: Containing the Adventures of Captain John Farrago, and Teague O'Regan, His Servant
reliability_notes: Newlin's variorum college edition, which reproduces the text of the separate parts of Brackenridge's novel as first published while collating them against the later revised issues, with introduction and notes. It predates modern scholarly editing of the 1805 and later revisions, so its apparatus is now dated even though its text remains convenient.

title: Poems
reliability_notes: The first volume of verse by the elder Dana (1787-1879), printed in Boston and the book that established his reputation among the second generation of American poets, including the poems later gathered with prose in his collected writings. This author is the father of the author of Two Years Before the Mast, and the two Danes' works are easily confused in catalogues.

title: Hobomok: A Tale of Early Times (Broadview Edition)
reliability_notes: The first critical edition of Child's 1824 novel of colonial Massachusetts, with introduction, explanatory notes and documentary appendices including Child's own letters and contemporary reviews. It is a single-volume Broadview edition rather than part of a collected Child, and its date should be given as the edition's own since the novel first appeared in 1824.
